salary-calculator.assumptionNote: Assumes 52 paid weeks per year and 260 working days. Does not subtract taxes, benefits, or unpaid time off. Gross pay only.
benefits: Converts confusing job offers - hourly vs salary - into the same language instantly.
Shows what each pay period actually pays, which helps with monthly budgeting.
Reveals the true hourly rate of a salaried job, including how overtime changes it.

faqs.a: Use the annual tab, enter $52,000 and 40 hours: it shows $25.00 an hour. The honest comparison also needs benefits: health insurance, retirement match, and paid time off can be worth 20 to 30% on top of salary.
faqs.q: Is $25 an hour the same as a $52,000 salary?

faqs.a: Multiply by 2,080 (40 hours x 52 weeks) for full-time. So $30 an hour is $62,400 a year. For part-time, use your actual hours: $30 x 25 hours x 52 weeks = $39,000.
faqs.q: How do I convert hourly to salary quickly?

faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by 2,080 (40 x 52) for a rough gross annual figure, then subtract roughly 20 to 30% for taxes depending on your bracket and state. For a real number, use the take-home paycheck calculator.
faqs.q: How do I estimate my take-home pay?

faqs.a: Salaried pay usually keeps coming during paid holidays and sick days, while hourly pay often stops. An hourly worker also misses pay during unpaid gaps. Over a year, a $52,000 salary can be worth noticeably more than $25 an hour with patchy hours.
faqs.q: Does salary beat hourly at the same rate?

faqs.a: Divide the annual salary by 2,080 for the 40-hour equivalent. $80,000 / 2,080 = $38.46 an hour. If you actually work 50 hours a week (2,600 hours a year), the real rate is $80,000 / 2,600 = $30.77 an hour - which is why hours matter.
faqs.q: How do I find the hourly rate of a salary?

faqs.a: No. This calculator shows gross pay before any deductions. Net (take-home) pay is always lower, sometimes much lower, depending on taxes, retirement contributions, and insurance premiums.

salary-calculator.formula:
Annual = hourly rate x hours per week x 52.
Monthly = annual / 12. Biweekly = annual / 26. Weekly = annual / 52. Daily = annual / 260.
Hourly (from salary) = annual / (hours per week x 52).
howTo: Choose your starting point: Hourly if you know your rate, Annual if you know your salary.
Enter your hourly rate or annual salary, plus your usual hours per week.
All six pay-period figures update instantly: hourly, daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, annual.
Use the breakdown to compare job offers or to set a monthly budget from an hourly wage.
keyFacts: Full-time is usually 40 hours a week x 52 weeks = 2,080 working hours a year.
Annual pay = hourly rate x hours per week x 52.
Biweekly pay (every 2 weeks) means 26 paychecks a year; monthly pay means 12.
Daily pay here assumes 260 working days (52 weeks x 5 days).
These are gross figures - before taxes, insurance, and retirement deductions.

salary-calculator.quickAnswer: To convert hourly to salary, multiply by hours per week and 52 weeks: $25 an hour at 40 hours a week is 25 x 40 x 52 = $52,000 a year. That breaks down to $4,333.33 a month, $2,000 every two weeks, $1,000 a week, and $200 a day. To go the other way, divide the salary by (hours per week x 52): $52,000 at 40 hours is $25.00 an hour. These are gross figures, before taxes.
